1What You Will Learn

  • State the CNCF cloud native definition and its example technologies
  • Compare a monolith with microservices, and recognize twelve-factor and resilience ideas
  • Describe serverless, event-driven design and open standards
  • Match the personas: developer, platform engineer, SRE, DevOps, security, FinOps

2The CNCF cloud native definition and its technologies

Running case

Harbor Books Rethinks Its Design

  • The shop began as one program, and it is now split into storefront, catalog, orders and more
  • The team wants each part to fail and recover alone, and the order-confirmation job to run only when needed
  • A platform team offers self-service tools, and a site reliability engineer (SRE) watches production
  • In this module you learn the vocabulary behind these choices

The CNCF Cloud Native Definition Moving

  • Cloud native practices let organizations build and run workloads in public, private and hybrid clouds, at scale, in a repeatable way
  • Its marks: loosely coupled systems that interoperate, and that are secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable
  • Typical examples: serverless, declarative APIs, containers, microservices, service meshes, multi-tenancy and immutable infrastructure; the list is non-exhaustive
  • As of 30 October 2026: the current definition is version 1.1, approved in February 2024

Exam tip: Loosely coupled, plus secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable.

3Monolith versus microservices, twelve-factor ideas, resilience (retries, timeouts, circuit breakers)

Monolith versus Microservices

  • Monolith: all functionality in one deployable program; the simplest place to start, but harder to maintain as it grows
  • Microservices: independent services, each focused on one function, that appear to the user as one application
  • Services can change and be released faster; the price is more parts to network, observe and secure (Module 6, Module 8 and Module 13)
  • A monolith is usually tightly coupled; microservices aim to be loosely coupled

Exam tip: A monolith is one program; microservices are many small services.

Twelve-Factor Ideas and Resilience Beyond the curriculum

Idea What it says
Config in the environment settings that vary between deploys live outside the code
Stateless processes the app runs as one or more stateless processes
Disposability processes start and stop at a moment's notice: fast startup, graceful shutdown
Logs as event streams the app writes events to its output, and the platform collects them
Timeout how long to wait for a reply, so a call succeeds or fails in a predictable time
Retry try again a limited number of times after a transient failure
Circuit breaker stop calling a failing service once a limit is reached
  • A service mesh (Module 6) can add timeouts, retries and circuit breakers without code changes

Exam tip: Retries heal blips; a circuit breaker stops hammering a failing service.

4Serverless, functions, event-driven design, autoscaling as an architecture idea

Serverless, Functions and Event-Driven Design Archived topic

  • Serverless: servers are abstracted away from you, you pay per use, and scaling is automatic
  • Knative Serving and OpenFaaS run serverless-style functions and containers on Kubernetes; OpenFaaS can scale to zero
  • Autoscaling adds and removes capacity by itself (Module 5); serverless platforms go further and can scale to zero
  • Event-driven design: components react to events, which are changes of state
  • CloudEvents describes event data in a common format, for interoperability

Exam tip: Serverless means no servers to manage; event-driven means reacting to changes.

5Open standards (OCI, CRI, CNI, CSI) and portability

Open Standards and Portability Archived topic

  • OCI: open specifications for the image format, runtime and distribution of containers
  • CRI: how the kubelet talks to a container runtime, for example containerd or CRI-O
  • CNI: how network plugins connect Pods; CSI: how storage drivers plug in
  • Open interfaces let you swap an implementation and keep workloads portable across hybrid and multi-cloud setups

Exam tip: OCI for images, CRI for runtimes, CNI for networks, CSI for storage.

6Personas, platform engineering, developer portals, what the exam asks

Personas and Platform Engineering Archived topic

Persona Focus
Developer writes the application and ships it along the delivery path
Platform engineer builds self-service tools and workflows that developers use
SRE applies software engineering to operations, so that code running in production works
DevOps teams own the whole path from development to production operations
Security (DevSecOps) adds security responsibilities to that path (Module 8)
FinOps shared financial accountability for technology spend between engineering, finance and business
  • Backstage, hosted by the CNCF, is a framework for a developer portal that brings tools, services and documentation together

Exam tip: Platform engineers build self-service tools; SREs keep production reliable.

What the Exam Asks: Cloud Native Architecture

  • The definition: loosely coupled systems that are secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable; the technology list is non-exhaustive
  • Monolith or microservices: one deployable program, or independent services
  • Serverless or event-driven: no servers to manage and automatic scaling, or reacting to events
  • OCI, CRI, CNI or CSI: images, runtimes, networks or storage
  • SRE, DevOps or platform engineering: reliability in production, shared ownership, or self-service tools
  • Immutable infrastructure: replace rather than change; containers are the example

Exam tip: For an architecture question, match the term to the problem it solves.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1According to the CNCF definition, which properties characterize cloud native systems?

  • ATightly coupled systems that are cheap, portable, small and simple to operate, whatever they are built from
  • BMonolithic systems that are secure, scalable and run only in a public cloud
  • CLoosely coupled systems that are secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable
  • DOpen source systems that are free of charge and written in a single language
Show the answer

Answer: C. The definition describes loosely coupled systems that are secure, resilient, manageable, sustainable and observable. It names public, private and hybrid clouds, and does not require any one language or license.

S2Which statement compares a monolith with microservices correctly?

  • AA monolith is one deployable program, while microservices are independent services that each focus on one function
  • BA monolith runs in containers, while microservices run on virtual machines of a cloud, and neither runs anywhere else
  • CA monolith is split into services that share a database, while microservices are a single program
  • DA monolith is faster to change, while microservices are released once a year at most
Show the answer

Answer: A. A monolith holds all functionality in a single deployable program. Microservices break an application into independent services, each focused on a specific function, which can be changed and released faster.

S3Harbor Books wants an order-confirmation function that runs only when an order event arrives, and scales down to zero otherwise. Which fits best?

  • AA DaemonSet, which keeps one copy of the function running on every node all the time
  • BA StatefulSet with a PersistentVolume for each replica, so that the function keeps its state between orders
  • CA Deployment with a fixed number of replicas that wait for requests around the clock
  • DA serverless platform such as OpenFaaS, which runs functions on events and can scale to zero
Show the answer

Answer: D. Serverless platforms run functions on demand, scale automatically and can scale to zero, so nothing runs between orders. The other objects keep a fixed set of Pods running all the time.

S4Which standard defines how the kubelet talks to a container runtime?

  • ACNI, the Container Network Interface, which defines how network plugins connect Pods to the cluster network
  • BCRI, the Container Runtime Interface used between the kubelet and the runtime
  • CCSI, which defines how storage systems are exposed to containers
  • DCloudEvents, which defines a common format for describing event data
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Container Runtime Interface is how the kubelet talks to a runtime such as containerd or CRI-O. CNI is for networking, CSI for storage and CloudEvents for event data.

S5Which role builds self-service tools and workflows so that developers can ship software faster?

  • AA site reliability engineer, who makes sure that code running in production works properly
  • BA FinOps practitioner, who shares financial accountability for technology spend
  • CA platform engineer, who builds a self-service platform for developers
  • DA security engineer, who adds security responsibilities to the delivery path
Show the answer

Answer: C. Platform engineering builds tools and processes, like a self-service station, that empower developers. SREs focus on production reliability, FinOps on cost accountability and DevSecOps on security.
